paragraphs: For the next trip, the organizer wrote the planned date of the condition check beside the name of the person responsible. She also noted which source would be consulted and how members would hear about a change. The plan described a task that still had to be done, rather than making the presence of a box on a form look like a completed check.

After receiving new information, the group kept both the earlier plan and the reason for revising it. Members could then see which assumption had changed. They did not conclude that the bridge route would never need checking either. A better record helped them distinguish what they remembered, what had recently been reported, and what remained uncertain. The lesson was to use experience to organize further questions, while leaving room to revise a decision when the evidence changed.
rationale: 間接疑問・関係節・動名詞・受動態を読み、時系列の接続と予定した確認・完了した確認の区別を理解する。

paragraphs: For the next exercise, the class asked readers to describe the kind of story they expected before showing them the relevant scene. The students compared those expectations with the advertisement's intended message. They did not ask only whether the line sounded exciting. One reader had understood the conflict but expected a cheerful ending that the group had never meant to promise. The group revised that part without revealing the ending itself. They kept a note of the misunderstanding beside the new wording so that a later designer could see the reason for the change. An accurate quotation remained one possible tool, but it was no longer treated as a complete explanation of a book. The question was what a new reader would reasonably expect from the whole presentation, including the words that surrounded the quotation and the details that had been left out.

paragraphs: Before planning another evening, the club asked visitors which part of the experience they could still describe. Some remembered a shape they had drawn, while others remembered a question discussed beside the telescope. The sketches did not prove that every visitor had understood every explanation. They gave the members a starting point for asking what had stayed with people and what had remained confusing.

The club also checked whether visitors who did not want to draw had another way to record a thought. Guides offered a place for a short written note and accepted spoken descriptions during the discussion. The aim was not to turn an evening of observing into a test of drawing skill. It was to leave enough time for visitors to notice, describe, and connect an observation with a question. Fewer targets could support that purpose when the time was used thoughtfully.
rationale: 関係節・間接疑問・動名詞・不定詞を読み、観察→修正→振り返りの順と記録が示す理解の範囲を理解する。

paragraphs: For the next change, the owner asked a new customer to match each price label to the product it described. One label stood between two baskets, so the customer could not tell which loaf it belonged to. Staff moved it beside the correct basket and checked the arrangement again. They also added a short heading to the process board, making clear that it explained the large loaf rather than every item in the shop. The extra explanation remained available to interested readers without hiding the basic choice. At the end of the week, staff noted the questions that still came up instead of assuming that fewer repeated questions meant complete understanding. A quiet customer might have understood the display, or might simply have left without asking. The owner treated the reduced number of questions as useful evidence, but kept checking what customers could actually find and explain.
rationale: 関係節・間接疑問・分詞を読み、情報分離の時系列と質問数の減少だけでは分からない利用者の理解を理解する。

paragraphs: For a second role-play, the students gave the revised agreement to a group that had not helped write it. Those readers could find the parts list, but one example still left unclear when a borrower should report a missing piece. The writers added a concrete point in the process and asked the readers to explain it in their own words.

They kept the question and the revision together as a record of how an apparently clear rule could need another check. The classroom exercise did not show that a longer agreement would always work better. It showed the value of asking someone outside the writing group to use the text in a situation. The students also left space to record a new problem rather than assuming their examples covered everything. Shared understanding depended on a continuing chance to ask and explain, not merely on the number of words.
rationale: 関係節・間接疑問・不定詞・動名詞を読み、役割演技の順と具体例・外部の読み手による理解確認の限界を理解する。
